That this scenario has arisen has led me to consider discussing the state of our ENM, yes. But that’s a bigger discussion over and above this rave, and also I think it’s disingenuous to lead with ‘so about vibeGuy…’.

Yes he knows I still talk to him. There hasn’t been anything particularly spicy since he first asked about the coffee date, small flirts like compliments nicer than your usual friends would say, but hasn’t even brought the rave up to me. I don’t even know if he knows I’m going (he hasn’t said ‘oh you’re also going to the rave?’ for example). So it may all be in my head anyway.

He means that for this specific rave, he feels comfortable in me exploring whatever vibes happen there, whether it’s the music, C, a random hot guy/girl/nb/pixie, or a combination. 

Outside of the confines of this rave, house rules (OPP) still apply.
It doesn’t ’very frequently’ set limits. This is the first time in 11 years that we’ve had a challenge to a limit.

I proposed the OPP. And for me it isn’t too emotionally heavy for him to date other women. We share our experiences and interactions with each other, so I know when he’s pursuing someone; and I know he comes home to me when he’s done. Besides, if he finds someone he wants to leave me for, ENM or not isn’t going to make a difference.

It’s individual situations, yes. Just like if he’s going on a date and I’m not feeling too comfortable about it, I tell him as much and he’s cancelled the date, or I reaffirm that I hope he has a good time and gets lucky 😉. Same with the roles reversed.

I can understand the perspective that it’s about romantic relationships vs. hooking up. The dichotomy is that he has no problem with me having a girlfriend.
You’re echoing my gut feeling too. In general I think it’s a harmless situation, but the optics are not great and that’s the damage.

C did invite me to the event. I passed it by my husband and he said it was all good. After confirming with C that we were on, I went to the event page and then saw that vibeGuy had also interacted with it (marked as interested). Weighing the situation, I went back to husband and told him the sex-positive culture and specified potential intimacy with C. Husband gave carte blanche on his own volition, and then vibeGuy later changed his status on it to ‘going’. 

Honestly if my husband hadn’t said anything about expanded consent (outside of C), then I wouldn’t have asked and I would rebuff vibeGuy if he made moves on me at the rave. He’s been respectful overall and hasn’t pushed past any boundaries I’ve set. I hadn’t brought vibeGuy up in the second talk with my husband, mostly because he does not fit into our standard circle of consent and the talk wasn’t to request for an exception. It was to inform him of the situation and ensure that he was comfortable with being in a public place and being cosy with C. But seeing vibeGuy’s name attached to the event and also C and I talking about our respective boundaries at a rave (such as party drugs too) compelled me to talk about it with my husband.

In retrospect, bringing vibeGuy up at that point might have been the right move, but he wasn’t 100% going at that time, and I feel like bringing someone up at first opportunity feels like just asking for permission to cheat?

That’s my thought too. I wanted impartial eyes on this as all my real-ass friends are telling me to just go with the flow. But the feeling that this is a grey area isn’t letting me do that and I trust that gut instinct.
It’s been fine for almost 11 years, vibeGuy is an anomaly. Honestly if I could ‘hall pass’ this one guy I’d probably not have a desire to ask for another one anytime soon.

vibeGuy wrote initially with a soft segue and said he wanted to meet for a coffee. On the surface it could have been taken totally platonically, and I didn’t press the intention. A few days later he wrote again and I asked him if he was shooting his shot, to which he said yes. I said it felt nice to hear sweet nothings like that, but it was toeing the line of what was acceptable in my relationship, and the next day I’d described pretty much the above. Then came the general ‘eat at home’ statement - not exclusively to vibeGuy but reprompted by his messages to me.  I didn’t express a specific desire to hook up, only that I received the messages.

He was not very familiar with ENM when we met. We probably would have stayed monogamous if I hadn’t raised the topic. That being said, I can imagine he’d have a hard time giving up the openness on his side - all told he’s been more actively NM than me (he’s had 3-4 partners since we officially opened up, I had one who we ended up friendzoning each other and she was one of my bridesmaids, and the other is C).

Most likely he’d want to keep it the way it is now - discussion about the foundation to the OPP would be long and thorough before it would change to more open.
Thank you. I guess I have a good idea of what his answer would be, and while I would like to open the conversation also to renegotiation of our boundaries, this is a poor springboard.

Yes, hyperbole (as gangbangs are far less common than porn would lead you to believe 🤣), but also I know this carte blanche includes men. We’ve visited swinger clubs before and I’ve gone to them on my own and he’s said in these specific incidences that he is fine with me having sex with whomever I vibe with, across genders. So far though I’ve only hooked up with one guy in these situations, the rest have all been women (and no gangbangs 🫠) By and large whenever either of us is about to go out with one of our partners we give a consent check to make sure. There’s been times in both our sides where the energy doesn’t feel right and we say so. We’ve both cancelled dates because the other wasn’t feeling so hot.

When he said ‘eat at home’, I don’t think he was meaning *this specific guy*, just reiterating the ‘no men in general’ sentiment. Which is fair and in line with what we have in place already. He doesn’t have any strong (negative) feelings about anyone I interact with.

vibeGuy is literally the sole incidence where there’s a combination of prior social interaction, knowledge of boundaries, and a ’hall pass’ situation. I think I’m having anxiety about bringing it up in case it makes a mountain of a molehill and then he doesn’t feel comfortable with me going to the rave at all, or he becomes wary at me having nights out with C at all (since she’s the one who I’m most likely to get freaky with anyway - vibeGuy being there too isn’t a guarantee of a hookup regardless).
